question: Who among the following first argued that in the face of high deficits, people save more?
solution:
The correct answer is __**David Ricardo.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **David Ricardo** first argued in the face of high deficits, people save more.
 
• The** law of comparative advantage** is popularly attributed to English political economist David Ricardo.
 
• His book **“On the Principles of Political Economy and Taxation” was **written in 1817.
 
• Comparative advantage is an economy's ability to produce a particular good or service at a lower opportunity cost than its trading partners.
 
• A comparative advantage gives a company the ability to sell goods and services at a lower price than its competitors and realize stronger sales margins.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Adam Smith was a Scottish economist also known as the Father of economics or the Father of Capitalism.
 
• Amartya Sen is a world-renowned economist awarded the 1998 Nobel Prize.
 
 
• He has propounded "the concept of public welfare economics".
 
 
 
• Good Economics for a Hard Time was written by Abhijit V Banerjee and Esther Duflo.
 
 
• In this book Nobel laureates Abhijit Banerjee and Esther Duflo debunk myths about migration.
